MUQATIL:7:31-35/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:31-35/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:31-35/r6.claim: Each nation has an appointed time for punishment, which cannot be delayed or brought forward; this responds to their demand for punishment.

TAB-FULL:v10p164#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p164#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p164#2/r1.claim: The verse threatens polytheists who excuse indecency by ancestral custom and falsely claim God commanded it, recalling the destruction of earlier nations that rejected messengers and persisted in associating partners with God. Each nation has an appointed time for punishment, which it can neither delay nor hasten by an hour.

ZAJJAJ:v2p334/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p334/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p334/r1.claim: An appointed term is a fixed time; ‘an hour’ names the shortest unit of time, so they cannot be delayed or advanced even by less than an hour.

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1472/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1472/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1472/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas asks which forefather was oldest, hears that it was Adam, and points out that God addresses humanity as children of Adam.

NAHHAS:v2p123/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p123/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p123/r3.claim: The appointed time is known to God; ساعة is an adverb, showing the slain die at their appointed time.

THALABI:v4p230/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p230/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p230/r6.claim: Each community has a fixed term, also interpreted as the time punishment arrives; once it ends, people can neither delay nor hasten it.

THALABI:v4p230/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p230/r7.speaker: ابن سيرين
THALABI:v4p230/r7.claim: Ibn Sirin reads the word as the plural ‘their appointed times.’

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p220/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p220/r1.speaker: جويبر
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p220/r1.claim: Juwair says each nation has a divine decree concerning its happiness or misery, punishment or mercy; other views make its term a prophet sent to command obedience or its allotted lifespan.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p220/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p220/r2.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p220/r2.claim: Muadh ibn Jabal interprets each nation's appointed term as a prophet who calls it to obedience and forbids disobedience.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p220/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p220/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p220/r3.claim: Another possible meaning is the period a nation remains in its religion before introducing disagreement.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p220/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p220/r4.speaker: جويبر
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p220/r4.claim: When the appointed term arrives, it may refer either to death or to the punishment of a nation, according to Juwair.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p220/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p220/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p220/r5.claim: The term cannot be lengthened or shortened, or the punishment brought forward or delayed.

QUSHAYRI:v1p331/r17.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p331/r17.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p331/r17.claim: Every community has a fixed term; when it ends, its condition ends too, whether prosperity or hardship.

QUSHAYRI:v1p331/r18.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p331/r18.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p331/r18.claim: The sunset and dawn illustrate how one spiritual condition ends as another begins, with darkness accumulating until dawn and then disappearing.

QUSHAYRI:v1p331/r19.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p331/r19.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p331/r19.claim: Do not rely on permissive conjecture when messengers warn: God needs nothing, yet accounts for every small or large act; deniers face humiliation and pain.

QUSHAYRI:v1p331/r20.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p331/r20.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p331/r20.claim: Felicity or misery is fixed by prior decree; grace may rescue the predestined fortunate even from Hell, while wrath can remove the predestined wretched even from Paradise.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p110/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p110/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p110/r1.claim: Ajal is the appointed time that ends a period of respite.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p110/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p110/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p110/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, and Muqatil take the term here as the time for punishment: it cannot be delayed or brought forward once due; al-Hasan specifies annihilation, and Muqatil says it follows their demand for punishment.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p110/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p110/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p110/r3.claim: The author prefers the punishment deadline because the verse says every community has a term, rather than every individual.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p110/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p110/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p110/r4.claim: The alternative is each person's lifespan; 'community' could describe the near-equal lifespans of people in each era as one shared term.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p111/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p111/r1.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p111/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj says they are not delayed even by less than an hour; the hour is named because it is the smallest time-unit word.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p111/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p111/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p111/r2.claim: Although advancing a deadline after it arrives seems impossible, Arabic can say winter has come when its onset approaches; thus they are not delayed after expiry or advanced as expiry nears.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p111/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p111/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p111/r3.claim: The phrase 'when their term comes' can cover both the end of the term and its approaching end.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:34-35/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:34-35/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:34-35/r1.claim: Every community has an appointed time for punishment and destruction; when it comes, it cannot be delayed or advanced by even an hour.

JISHUMI:v4p2548/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2548/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2548/r3.claim: An umma is a group united by a shared meaning or purpose; the term derives from intending or aiming.

JISHUMI:v4p2548/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2548/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2548/r4.claim: An ajal is a thing's duration and the appointed time at which it ends, including a debt's term or a lifespan.

JISHUMI:v4p2548/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2548/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2548/r5.claim: Isti qdām is derived from advancing; it can mean to precede or to seek to advance, as in the verse about those who come first and last.

JISHUMI:v4p2548/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2548/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2548/r6.claim: Istiʾkhār means seeking delay and derives from ākhir, what comes after the first; the source gives two different pronunciations for a phrase meaning later.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p226#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p226#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p226#2/r5.claim: An الأمة’s appointed term is its span of life, food, and drink; Ibn Abbas, Ata, and al-Hasan understand it as the time fixed for punishment.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p226#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p226#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p226#2/r6.claim: When the term comes and their food ends, they can neither delay nor advance it; the verse came after they asked for punishment.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p395#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p395#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p395#2/r1.claim: Sāʿa names the smallest piece of time but stands for every part of time, as 'not even an atom's weight' does in Qur'an 4:40.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p395#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p395#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p395#2/r2.claim: The apparent conflict with promises to delay punishment if people believe in Qur'an 14:10 and 71:4 is resolved by the Sunni view that each person has one fixed term: those destined to disbelieve meet it sooner, while believers reach their appointed later term.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p395#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p395#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p395#2/r3.claim: Noah did not know which people belonged to either group, so he called everyone to salvation; Muhammad likewise calls all people to Paradise while knowing some will disbelieve, like a prisoner offered conversion or death.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p395/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p395/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p395/r5.claim: Every community or group has a fixed term for punishment when it disbelieves or disobeys; the warning applies to Muhammad's community as well.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p395/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p395/r6.speaker: الحسن، ابن سيرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p395/r6.claim: Al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin read the word for terms in the plural; Abu al-Fath says plural is more apparent because every person has a term, while the singular is a collective genus.

TABRISI:7:33-34/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:33-34/r10.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:7:33-34/r10.claim: Mujāhid identifies fornication as hidden immorality and nudity during circumambulation as its manifest form.

TABRISI:7:33-34/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:33-34/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:33-34/r11.claim: The author summarizes the ugliness of the prohibited acts before detailing the categories in the following discussion.

TABRISI:7:33-34/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:33-34/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:33-34/r3.claim: An ummah is a community sharing one purpose; an appointed term is the set time when a period ends, after a span such as a debt, provision, promise, or lifespan.

TABRISI:7:33-34/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:33-34/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:33-34/r9.claim: The phrase manifest and hidden means what is public and what is concealed.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p192/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p192/r1.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p192/r1.claim: The verse was revealed after people asked the Prophet to bring punishment.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p192/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p192/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p192/r2.claim: An umma's appointed term may mean the deadline for punishment or its lifespan.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p192/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p192/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p192/r4.claim: “Not an hour” means not even less than an hour; an hour is mentioned as the smallest named interval.

RAZI-FULL:v14p56/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p56/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p56/r1.claim: Every nation or person has a fixed term; when it arrives death is unavoidable, a warning intended to strengthen observance of religious duties.

RAZI-FULL:v14p56/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p56/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن ومقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v14p56/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, Hasan, and Muqatil say each nation that rejected its messenger was given a deadline until it deserved the decisive destruction appointed for it; Razi prefers this reading because the verse says every nation, not every person.

RAZI-FULL:v14p56/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p56/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p56/r3.claim: Razi says the nation-wide deadline is stronger than the lifespan reading: it fits the wording and need not imply that every nation, including Muhammad's community, actually receives total extermination.

RAZI-FULL:v14p56/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p56/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p56/r4.claim: If the term means an individual's lifespan, a person killed dies at the appointed time; this does not make God unable to lengthen or shorten life, but states what He has decreed rather than making Him an involuntary cause.

RAZI-FULL:v14p56/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p56/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p56/r5.claim: Not advancing or delaying even an hour means no delay or precedence by any smaller amount; an hour is named as the smallest named unit of time.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:34/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:34/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:34/r1.claim: Each community has a fixed term known to God; the hour is used because it is the smallest named time, and a person’s appointed death cannot be delayed or advanced.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:34/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:34/r2.speaker: ابن سيرين
QURTUBI-FULL:7:34/r2.claim: Ibn Sirin reads the phrase with the plural ‘their appointed times.’

QURTUBI-FULL:7:34/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:34/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:34/r3.claim: A person’s ajal is the time God knows the living person will certainly die, not a time that is impossible for God to delay in power.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:34/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:34/r4.speaker: كثير من المعتزلة
QURTUBI-FULL:7:34/r4.claim: Most Mu‘tazilites, with a few exceptions, say a murdered person dies before the appointed term and would otherwise have lived; Qurtubi calls this wrong.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:34/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:34/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:34/r5.claim: The victim dies because God takes the soul at the moment of the blow, not because the killer’s act independently causes death; retaliation punishes the killer’s transgression and prevents social ruin.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:34-35/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:34-35/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:34-35/r1.claim: Each nation has a fixed term, either its lifespan or the appointed time when punishment descends; the warning is directed to Mecca's people.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:34-35/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:34-35/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:34-35/r2.claim: When the term ends, no one can delay it or bring it forward by even an hour, or even ask for either because of the terror.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p10#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p10#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p10#2/r1.claim: Every nation has a fixed time for annihilating punishment if it does not believe; this threatens Mecca with a divinely known term, as earlier nations were punished.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p10#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p10#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p10#2/r2.claim: When the term arrives it cannot be advanced or delayed; 'an hour' is used as the smallest ordinary unit of reprieve.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r11.claim: The verse warns Meccans that, like earlier peoples, their punishment has a fixed time known to God if they disobey their Lord.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r12.claim: Other interpretations take each nation's appointed term as its worldly life span, after which it meets the record of its true or false deeds.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r13.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r13.claim: He says “community” here means a faction or group, a word commonly used for many people.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r14.claim: Another definition allows a community to be small or large, even a single person, as in the report about Quss ibn Sāʿida being raised alone as a community.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r15.claim: The term “term” is singular because it is a generic noun, communities of an era have similar deeds, or the phrase means one term for every individual.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r16.speaker: الحسن وابن سيرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r16.claim: They read the word for appointed terms in the plural.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r17.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r17.claim: He explains “an hour” as the shortest time in ordinary speech, meaning the nearest or briefest moment.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r18.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r18.claim: He says “hour” denotes a small unit of time while intending the totality of its parts.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r19.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r19.claim: A future negative after “when” may answer it with or without a prefixed fāʾ; without it, an omitted subject makes the response nominal, which requires fāʾ or sudden idhā.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r20.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p44/r20.claim: Al-Ḥawfī's coordination of “nor do they precede” with “they do not lag” fails: a future event cannot determine that a past event did not precede it, as the Zuhayr poem illustrates.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p46/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p46/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p46/r9.claim: He reads “nor do they precede” as a new report that people do not get ahead of their appointed term; together the clauses deny both preceding and delaying it.

SAMIN-DURR:7:34#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:34#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:34#2/r1.claim: لا يستقدمون is a fresh clause: people do not outstrip their appointed term and must complete it, just as they cannot delay beyond it.

SAMIN-DURR:7:34#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:34#2/r2.speaker: الحوفي وغيره
SAMIN-DURR:7:34#2/r2.claim: Al-Hawfi and others coordinate لا يستقدمون with لا يستأخرون, but the author rejects this because إذا governs future events, whereas advancing would precede the term.

SAMIN-DURR:7:34#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:34#2/r3.speaker: الواحدي
SAMIN-DURR:7:34#2/r3.claim: Al-Wahidi explains the coordination by saying that Arabs call an approaching event as already arrived: no delay once the term ends and no advance as it approaches.

SAMIN-DURR:7:34#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:34#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:34#2/r4.claim: Al-Wahidi's explanation assumes coordination with لا يستأخرون, which is also the apparent basis of exegetes' statements.

SAMIN-DURR:7:34/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:34/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:34/r1.claim: The phrase means every community has a term; no omitted مُضاف meaning each individual is needed, and the verse has broader scope than an individual lifespan.

SAMIN-DURR:7:34/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:34/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SAMIN-DURR:7:34/r2.claim: Some interpret the phrase as each person from a community having a lifespan.

SAMIN-DURR:7:34/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:34/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:34/r3.claim: A grammatical observation says comparable clauses elsewhere usually put fa before إذا, except in Yunus; the fa links successive connected clauses.

SAMIN-DURR:7:34/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:34/r4.speaker: الحسن وابن سيرين
SAMIN-DURR:7:34/r4.claim: Al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin read آجالهم in the plural.

SAMIN-DURR:7:34/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:34/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:34/r5.claim: لا يستأخرون answers إذا; a negative present-tense clause may appear with or without an introductory fa.

SAMIN-DURR:7:34/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:34/r6.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:7:34/r6.claim: Al-Shaykh argues that a subject placed between fa and the verb makes a nominal sentence, which must be introduced by fa or إذا فجائية.

SAMIN-DURR:7:34/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:34/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:34/r7.claim: ساعة is an adverb of time used figuratively to indicate a very short interval.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p409#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p409#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p409#2/r1.claim: Each community and generation has an appointed time; when it arrives, it cannot be delayed or brought forward even by an hour.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p27/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p27/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p27/r10.claim: The final clause may attach to the whole conditional or to the fixed term, which God set with full knowledge and without acquiring new knowledge.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p27/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p27/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p27/r11.claim: Alternatively, the clause links to 7:24: humanity will multiply into communities, each with its own term rather than being destroyed collectively at one time.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p27/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p27/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p27/r8.claim: Every community has a fixed term; God does not hasten its end because He fears loss or harm, and any opposition ultimately harms only its people.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p27/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p27/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p27/r9.claim: The hour means the shortest conceivable time in ordinary speech, and no community can delay or advance its appointed term.

DURR-FULL:v3p447/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p447/r5.speaker: أبو الدرداء
DURR-FULL:v3p447/r5.claim: Kinship does not literally extend a fixed lifespan; rather, righteous descendants' prayers reach a deceased person and extend his trace or benefit in the grave.

DURR-FULL:v3p447/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p447/r6.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v3p447/r6.claim: Hasan calls it foolish to ask God to lengthen someone's life, since once the term arrives it cannot be delayed or advanced.

DURR-FULL:v3p447/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p447/r7.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v3p447/r7.claim: Ka'b says God could defer Umar's term if he prayed; citing 35:11, al-Zuhri explains every lifespan is recorded and may be deferred or reduced before its appointed arrival, never after it arrives.

BURSEVI:v3p119#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p119#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p119#2/r1.claim: Each destroyed nation has a fixed term for annihilation; the singular pronoun means each nation has its own appointed time.

BURSEVI:v3p119#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p119#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p119#2/r2.claim: When its hour arrives, they cannot delay at all; ‘hour’ figures a tiny span and the emphatic form signals helplessness despite wanting delay.

BURSEVI:v3p119#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p119#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p119#2/r3.claim: They also cannot arrive before the appointed time.

BURSEVI:v3p119#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p119#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p119#2/r4.claim: A Persian couplet says that when a person's appointed term comes, it cannot be delayed or advanced.

BURSEVI:v3p119#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p119#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p119#2/r5.claim: A king abandons asceticism for worldly rule and builds a palace; a voice reminds him death is fixed, so he gives up entertainments, repents, and dies repeating ‘death.’

BURSEVI:v3p119#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p119#3/r1.speaker: السعدي
BURSEVI:v3p119#3/r1.claim: Saʿdī's Persian verses warn that worldly houses become ruins and gardens thorn growth.

BURSEVI:v3p119#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p119#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p119#3/r2.claim: In the inward reading, each community of travelers to God, Paradise, or Hell has a fixed period and respite assigned by God.

BURSEVI:v3p119#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p119#3/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v3p119#3/r3.claim: The Najmī taʾwīl treats the fixed term as reassurance to God's friends and a threat disciplining His enemies.

ALUSI-FULL:v8p112#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p112#3/r1.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v8p112#3/r1.claim: Al-Hasan, with reports from Ibn Abbas and Muqatil, takes each nation's term as an appointed time for its destruction; the statement warns Mecca of punishment at a time known to God.

ALUSI-FULL:v8p112#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p112#3/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v8p112#3/r2.claim: Other interpretations take the term as a set respite before punishment, or as the time of death, construing 'each nation' as each individual of the nation; the author notes the death-time reading needs no omitted wording.

ALUSI-FULL:v8p112#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p112#3/r3.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v8p112#3/r3.claim: The pronoun 'their' can refer to the nations implied by 'every nation' or to each nation itself; explicit repetition of 'term' emphasizes each community's particular appointed time.

ALUSI-FULL:v8p112#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p112#3/r4.speaker: ابن سيرين
ALUSI-FULL:v8p112#3/r4.claim: Ibn Sirin recites آجالهم in the plural; Ibn Jinni favors that form, while the singular may denote the class collectively.

ALUSI-FULL:v8p112#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p112#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p112#3/r5.claim: The arrival of the term means its approach or completion; ساعة is a tiny interval, not the astronomers' fixed hour or the variable hour used by jurists, and the expression means no delay whatsoever, with the form implying incapacity to delay.

ALUSI-FULL:v8p113/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p113/r1.speaker: الحوفي
ALUSI-FULL:v8p113/r1.claim: Al-Hufi and others parse 'nor do they advance' as coordinated with 'nor are they delayed'; an objection says advancing after the term arrives is logically impossible and therefore redundant.

ALUSI-FULL:v8p113/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p113/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v8p113/r2.claim: Another parse coordinates the final clause with the conditional premise: each nation has a term, and it cannot advance at any point; al-Salakuti objects that restricting only the no-delay clause to the condition is not readily apparent.

ALUSI-FULL:v8p113/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p113/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p113/r3.claim: The author holds that coordination with the conditional clause is correct: God-determined timing cannot be changed, so the term can neither advance nor be delayed; the pairing also echoes the two kinds of unaccepted late repentance in 4:18.

ALUSI-FULL:v8p113/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p113/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p113/r4.claim: The interpretation that they cannot change the appointed time resembles 'no fresh or dry thing except in a record'; scholars also analyze whether a condition preceding the coordinated clause is shared by it.

ALUSI-FULL:v8p113/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p113/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p113/r5.claim: The no-delay clause comes first because the point is that the condemned cannot escape punishment; Yunus reverses the order to explain why destruction is delayed despite their deserving it, following the command to let them enjoy themselves for a while.

ELMALILI:7:32-34/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:32-34/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:32-34/r13.claim: Each community, nation, state, and even individual has an appointed period of respite before punishment or destruction; different wrongdoing may take different lengths of time to bring an end.

ELMALILI:7:32-34/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:32-34/r14.speaker: İbn Abbas ve ekser müfessirînin muhtârı
ELMALILI:7:32-34/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas's and most exegetes' preferred reading takes the appointed term here as the time for punishment or destruction, not a person's lifespan; thus a righteous community may endure until the world's end.

ELMALILI:7:32-34/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:32-34/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:32-34/r15.claim: When the appointed time comes, no one can delay or advance it even by a moment; only God knows its timing, so people should not be deceived by temporary respite but repent and obey promptly.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p104#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p104#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p104#2/r1.claim: Each nation's term is its collective lifespan, not each member's individual lifespan; the context and singular الأمة support this, while an individual term would name each person or living being.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p104#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p104#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p104#2/r2.claim: إذا usually marks future time and condition; the prefixed فاء supplies the consequence linkage, and fronting the time phrase emphasizes the appointed term.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p104#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p104#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p104#2/r3.claim: The singular أجل has generic force, as its attachment to a plural pronoun indicates.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p104#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p104#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p104#2/r4.claim: Repeating أجل instead of using a pronoun reinforces the ruling and makes the clause stand alone like a proverb.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p104#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p104#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p104#2/r5.claim: The forms يستأخرون and يستقدمون mean delay and advance, with the extra letters serving emphasis; people cannot alter God's appointed term.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p104#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p104#2/r6.speaker: أبو الشيص
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p104#2/r6.claim: Abu al-Shis's verse depicts being unable to move later or earlier, illustrating the image of being trapped by an unavoidable decree.

TABATABAI:7:26-36#8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:26-36#8/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:26-36#8/r4.claim: Asked about the appointed term, al-Sadiq says it is what has been assigned to the Angel of Death; the author links this to earlier reports on 6:2.

TABATABAI:7:34-35/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:34-35/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:34-35/r1.claim: The verse derives a general rule from the story: communities, like individuals, have appointed lifespans, and once their term arrives they cannot delay or advance it.

TABATABAI:7:34-35/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:34-35/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:34-35/r2.claim: He suggests 7:25 concerns the life and death of each person and community within humanity’s larger lifespan, while the earlier earthly provision lasts until humanity’s extinction or resurrection.

ASAD-NOTES:7:33#n25/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:33#n25/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:33#n25/r1.claim: Ummah can mean living beings and here means people; each community has a God-decreed life term during which it may accept or reject revealed guidance.

ASAD-NOTES:7:33#n26/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:33#n26/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:33#n26/r1.claim: Sa'ah can mean time absolutely or any fraction of time; here it means the smallest fraction, a single moment.

ASAD-NOTES:7:33#n27/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:33#n27/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:33#n27/r1.claim: The literal phrase means that each person receives their allotted share of the divine decree, including good or bad fortune during life.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p31/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p31/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p31/.claim: A nation’s fixed term warns Quraysh that delayed punishment is not acquittal; God’s established destruction of rebellious peoples will come when their appointed time arrives, without delay or advance.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p31/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p31/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p31/.claim: An individual’s term is measured in time units, while a nation’s term depends on the decline of its faith and morals until it reaches a limit warranting destruction.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p31/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p31/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p31/.claim: God alone knows when an individual or nation reaches its end and when continued existence conflicts with divine wisdom.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p31/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p31/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p31/.claim: Sending a messenger completes the communication of truth to a nation; if it then denies the messenger, God destroys it, a rule discussed further in Sūrah Yūnus.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:34/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:34/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:34/r1.claim: Verses 34–53 begin an extended depiction of the afterlife.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:34/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:34/r2.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:34/r2.claim: Because the preceding section addresses Meccan pagans, ‘every community’ especially means groups that denied the Prophet and true religion; the verse warns and threatens them.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:34/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:34/r3.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:34/r3.claim: Ibn Ashur says the first ‘term’ is the respite given to rejecting communities and the second is its expiry and their end.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:34/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:34/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:34/r4.claim: As an act of mercy, God gives rejecting and rebellious communities time to reform, but those persisting in their old ways are inevitably punished when the term ends and cannot advance or delay that fate.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:34/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:34/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:34/r5.claim: The same divine law that brought pagan Arabs and earlier immoral, rebellious societies to ruin will eventually reach present and future deniers and oppressive states at their appointed time.

STUDYQURAN:7:34/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:34/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:34/r1.claim: Each community has a fixed term after which it ceases to exist on earth; the term cannot be advanced or delayed.

STUDYQURAN:7:34/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:34/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:34/r2.claim: The appointed term for communities is also referenced in several other verses.

STUDYQURAN:7:34/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:34/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:34/r3.claim: Individual people and humanity as a whole also have an appointed term concerning earthly life.
